correctness.rationale: The exact domain \(h>0\), \(r\ge0\) and one-dimensional Hausdorff normalization are explicit. For each feasible continuum meeting three disks, its length is no smaller than a three-terminal Steiner tree, itself bounded by \(\min_p\sum_i\operatorname{dist}(p,D_i)\); projection spokes supply the matching upper bound. Convexity and axis reflection reduce to a one-dimensional piecewise distance function, whose derivative has a unique free zero at \(y=1/\sqrt3\) and whose active interval is \( [\sqrt{\max\{r^2-1,0\}},\max\{h-r,0\}] \). A sharp minimal-enclosing-disk calculation handles zero length. Substituting the endpoints proves every branch and limiting boundary. The standalone checker passed 644 formula/projection cases and 20 finite 2D grid cases; a separate 200-case global optimizer stress test agreed to \(8\times10^{-11}\). Finite tests are supporting only; no all-optimizer uniqueness is claimed.

value.rationale: For the smallest noncollinear finite maximal-distance-minimizer family, the tolerance changes the actual optimal network topology. A complete all-radius two-continuous-parameter classification determines the exact length, constructs canonical minimizers, and finds the sharp height transitions \(1/\sqrt3\), \(1\), \(\sqrt3\), including the exceptional direct tripod-to-point collapse. The individual classical shapes and initial trimmed-tripod branch are explicitly credited; the genuinely valued fact is the full regime ordering and transition boundaries, beyond an isolated computation or cosmetic variant.
